title: Actual Evapotranspiration During Contrasting Wet and Dry Years in a Grazed Grassland on Fen Peat With Restricted Drainage
content:
ABSTRACT

Actual evapotranspiration (ETa) is a key component of ecosystem water, energy and carbon cycling, yet field-scale measurements from managed grasslands on fen peat remain limited, despite a growing interest in water table depth (WTD) management as a greenhouse gas (GHG) mitigation strategy. This study quantified ETa using eddy covariance over two climatically contrasting years (2023–2024) in an intensively managed grassland on fen peat in Ireland, which had a flume installed in field drains to limit the loss of water from the ecosystem. Annual ETa decreased by 29.6% from 373 ± 28.4 mm in 2023 to 263.0 ± 7.2 mm in 2024, despite similar air temperatures and available energy. Reference crop evapotranspiration (ET0) calculated using FAO-56 Penman–Monteith was comparable for both years (584 and 581 mm, respectively) while crop coefficient (Kc) also decreased from 0.63 to 0.45. Incoming shortwave radiation was the strongest predictor of ETa, while a tensor-product smooth revealed a significant joint nonlinear effect of vapour pressure deficit (VPD) and water-table depth (WTD) on ETa (EDF = 11.58, F = 27.95, p < 0.001), indicating that the influence of atmospheric demand varied with WTD. Maximum daily ETa occurred at intermediate WTD (50–70 cm below the surface), whereas near-saturated or deeper WTDs (> 70 cm below the surface) reduced ETa. These findings indicate that WTD can influence ETa by modifying vegetation response to atmospheric demand, highlighting how hydrological management of agricultural fens may influence vegetation water use, productivity and GHG mitigation strategies.
